notes: PSA 8.3 ng/mL. PI-RADS 2. PSAD 0.21. Prostate volume 40 mL. DRE nodus. csPCa 0.70.

note_sections.t: Re-evaluation of recently diagnosed low-grade prostate cancer to determine optimal management strategy.

Recently retired warehouse worker, now 64 years old, presents for urology follow-up following a prostate cancer diagnosis confirmed in May 2024. He reports no significant urinary symptoms, though his IPSS score is 17/35 indicating moderate lower urinary tract symptoms. He is married and lives in a multi-generational household with an adult child, with his spouse serving as his primary contact. He is an ex-smoker with a 23 pack-year history, having quit in 2014, and consumes approximately one unit of alcohol per week. His exercise routine consists mainly of gardening, with no structured physical activity. He has a history of vasectomy and inguinal hernia repair, and currently takes no active medications. He notes that the clinic is over 90 minutes away, making phone follow-up preferable when clinically appropriate.

On DRE, a nodule is palpable in the right peripheral zone of the prostate, consistent with clinical stage cT2. The prostate is non-tender and symmetrically enlarged. General examination is unremarkable with normal vital signs and no lymphadenopathy or abdominal masses.

admin: Lives >90 min from clinic; phone follow-up preferred where clinically safe.
